claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: For a nontrivial connected cograph, the canonical root operation is a join, and its join blocks are the complement-components. A singleton block is exactly a universal vertex. If there are at least two universal vertices, pairing two of them covers every closed neighborhood. If there are none, every block has at least two vertices; choosing a,b in one block and c,d in another gives disjoint pairs such that the second pair covers the first block and the first pair covers every other block. This is a pairing dominating set, so Remark 9 makes the component contextually equivalent to zero. These cases exhaust everything except a singleton and the exactly-one-universal case.
claims.witness: For root-join blocks A and D with |A|,|D| at least two, use pairs (a,b) in A and (c,d) in D. Every vertex of A belongs to N[c] intersection N[d], and every vertex outside A belongs to N[a] intersection N[b]. With two universal vertices, that universal pair alone suffices.
claims.search_method: Proved the canonical cotree case split directly, then exhaustively generated all 6,039 labeled cographs on at most six vertices; all 1,199 applicable connected cases had the stated pairing witness and exact values (0,0).

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: Let u be the unique universal vertex of a retained component C. A swap simulation shows that u weakly dominates every other move in C for either player, even with an arbitrary disjoint context: if the simulated owner of u is unchanged, the terminal coloring is unchanged; otherwise a Breaker-owned u makes the simulated or actual component score zero in the direction favorable to the player making the replacement. After Breaker takes u, the component has identically zero payoff and is equivalent to zero. After Maker takes u, |C-u| is at least two and the cograph C-u contains twins a,b. Applying Theorem 13 in both C with u Maker-owned and in C-u preassigns a to Maker and b to Breaker. The vertex u is spoiled by b, while every other closed-neighborhood condition is identical, proving contextual equivalence to C-u. Recursion therefore gives exactly the open-or-delete forest. Conversely, an internal forest node is realized as a new universal vertex joined to the disjoint union of its child realizations and a zero K2 ballast; the ballast makes the new vertex uniquely universal. The size is L+3I and the edge count is polynomial. Empty-child non-prize nodes are zero and may be omitted.
claims.witness: Forward transition: Maker taking u exposes R(C-u), while Breaker taking u deletes C. Reverse gadget for children H1,...,Ht is K1 joined with (H1 disjoint-union ... disjoint-union Ht disjoint-union K2).
claims.search_method: Established contextual dominance and the twin reduction symbolically. Exact bitmask minimax then matched the recursive forest value for every labeled cograph through six vertices, and matched the reverse construction for every canonical rooted forest through four nodes.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Let A be a prize-leaf game and Z the zero game. Inductively discard Z-children. An internal node with zero or one A-child has both starting-player values zero, hence is Z. With two A-children, their sum has value one for either starter and is therefore the constant-one game; opening the parent gives Maker one while Breaker deleting it gives zero, exactly the options of A. Thus every subtree labels as A or Z in constant time. If z top-level trees label A, the exact scores are ceil(z/2) and floor(z/2). Given the cotree/reduced forest, every node is visited once.
claims.witness: Bottom-up rule: a prize leaf labels A; an internal node labels A exactly when precisely two nonzero children label A, and labels Z otherwise.
claims.search_method: Proved the A/Z induction using contextual zero and constant-game equivalence, then exhaustively checked all 621 canonical outdegree-at-most-two forests through nine nodes by exact minimax.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For a multiset S of unopened star sizes and l exposed leaves, the unrestricted Bellman recurrence permits taking a leaf or acting on any star. A simultaneous strong induction on remaining nodes gives star-size monotonicity and, for j<=k, V_X(S union {j},l+k) >= V_X(S union {k},l+j) for either player to move. Opening the two distinguished stars leads to the same successor; leaf and other-star moves reduce to the induction hypothesis, while deleting a distinguished star uses size monotonicity. Hence Maker's best star-opening option is a largest star and Breaker's best deletion option is a largest star. The displayed two-parameter recurrence follows. Its bases are the exact alternating-pile values ceil(l/2) and floor(l/2), and it has O(rK)=O(n^2) reachable states after sorting.
claims.witness: For sorted k1<=...<=kr, the exact transitions are M(i,l)=max(1+B(i,l-1) when l>0, B(i-1,l+ki)) and B(i,l)=min(M(i,l-1) when l>0, M(i-1,l)), with the largest star ki used in each star transition.
claims.search_method: Checked the exchange induction against exact unrestricted minimax on 1,751,584 height-one states with total prize count at most 42, including 3,503,082 largest-star comparisons and 34,659,624 monotonicity/constant-pair relations; all passed using integers only.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: Exact minimax gives both P3 and K1,3 the standalone pair (1,0), but their behavior in the same disjoint context differs: P3 disjoint-union P3 has (1,1), whereas P3 disjoint-union K1,3 has (2,1). Therefore substitution based only on the standalone pair cannot preserve parent values, so that pair is not a sufficient compositional cotree state.
claims.witness: Concrete witness: P3 and K1,3 have identical standalone scores (1,0); using P3 as context produces respectively (1,1) and (2,1).
claims.search_method: Ran exact integer-bitmask minimax over all move sequences for the four stated graphs and graph unions.

target_evidence: The exact target requests either a polynomial-time algorithm for unrestricted cographs or a matching hardness theorem. The draft establishes neither: arbitrary reduced rooted forests remain unresolved. Its exact reduction, reverse realization, two infinite polynomial subclasses, and obstruction to a two-number cotree state are nevertheless material and correct progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate. The draft labels itself PARTIAL and its final writeup explicitly disclaims a complete classification; that claimed resolution is ACCURATE and does not overclaim target coverage.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source-input JSON and iteration-3 draft; did not use the web, retrieval data, receipts, prior runs, or verification reports.
